sections.title: Technology advisory
sections.subtitle: Turn business priorities into a practical technology roadmap.

backgroundImage.alt: Stakeholders reviewing a technology plan together

sections.heading: Make the right technology decisions before delivery begins
sections.body:
Linkfields connects business priorities with technology roadmaps, architecture assessments and product discovery, so you can prioritise investment and define the next delivery step.

Use advisory when competing priorities, application dependencies or an unclear product brief are holding up a programme. [Discuss your roadmap](#get-in-touch) with the business decision, current landscape and programme stage.

sections.heading: What your advisory engagement produces
sections.description: The scope is agreed around the decisions you need to make, with clear outputs to support investment approval and delivery planning.

items.title: Prioritised technology roadmap
items.description: A sequenced investment plan with dependencies, decision owners and approval gates.
items.bullets: Decision supported - what to fund first and what must happen before delivery

items.title: Architecture assessment
items.description: A current-state view, integration dependencies and target options with trade-offs.
items.bullets: Decision supported - which architecture fits the business and its constraints

items.title: Application portfolio rationalisation
items.description: A retain, modernise, replace or retire assessment linked to business capability.
items.bullets: Decision supported - where to reduce duplication and focus change

items.title: Cloud and data readiness
items.description: A readiness view covering workloads, data quality, access and governance dependencies.
items.bullets: Decision supported - which prerequisites need resolving before implementation

items.title: Product and solution discovery
items.description: A validated business brief, prioritised requirements and prototype findings where appropriate.
items.bullets: Decision supported - whether to proceed, revise or stop an idea

sections.heading: Agree the route from priorities to delivery

items.title: Align priorities
items.description: Bring business and technology stakeholders together around objectives, constraints and investment choices.
items.bullets: Output - agreed decision brief and success measures

items.title: Assess the landscape
items.description: Review architecture, applications, data and integration dependencies.
items.bullets: Output - current-state assessment and option constraints

items.title: Validate the options
items.description: Validate stakeholder assumptions with user research, technical assessment and prototype testing where appropriate.
items.bullets: Output - findings, trade-offs and a recommendation

items.title: Agree the roadmap
items.description: Sequence work and assign decision owners, dependencies and approval gates.
items.bullets: Output - prioritised roadmap and the next delivery decision

sections.heading: Turn the roadmap into delivery
sections.description: The agreed roadmap determines the delivery path. Software and accelerators are considered where relevant, not included in every assessment.

items.title: Linkworks
items.description: Consider composable enterprise applications where ERP or CRM does not fit.
items.bullets: Assessment question - can microservices, REST APIs and composable UI address the gap?

items.title: testoriumz
items.description: Consider continuous quality engineering when the roadmap includes application change.
items.bullets: Assessment question - what test automation and CI/CD assurance does the programme need?

items.title: Delivery accelerators
items.description: Consider reusable modernisation, integration, migration and release-assurance IP.
items.bullets: Assessment question - which reusable artefacts fit the agreed delivery scope?

sections.note: Products are available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without services. Product selection and licensing are agreed separately.

sections.heading: Make decisions with evidence and controls

items.title: Security and data boundaries
items.description: Identify sensitive information, access constraints and security-review requirements before assessment or prototype work.
items.bullets: Artefact - agreed access and information-handling requirements

items.title: Decision and approval record
items.description: Capture assumptions, option trade-offs, risk owners and the evidence needed at each investment gate.
items.bullets: Artefact - decision log and sign-off criteria

items.title: From decision to delivery
items.description: Example engagement pattern, not a completed client case: a fragmented application estate prompts a dependency assessment.
items.bullets:
Assessment - map duplicated capability and interfaces
Decision - prioritise a bounded modernisation tranche
Delivery change - resolve integration and regression prerequisites before the build

sections.note: Business capability: customer servicing. Proposed step: validate the integration boundary. Dependency: data ownership. Decision gate: architecture and security review. This is an example format, not client evidence.

items.title: What should we bring to discovery?
items.description: Share the business decision, programme stage, current applications and known constraints. Existing architecture diagrams, requirements and investment priorities help define the assessment scope.

items.title: Does advisory include implementation?
items.description: Advisory defines recommendations and the next delivery decision. Implementation is scoped separately across the relevant Linkfields portfolios; the roadmap can also support a client-led delivery programme.

items.title: How are prototypes and sensitive information handled?
items.description: Agree prototype scope, data access, information handling and review gates before work begins. We can agree an NDA before detailed discovery. Use only the data and environments authorised for the assessment.

items.title: Which commercial model fits?
items.description: Fixed Price suits defined assessments with agreed outputs; Time & Materials supports evolving discovery. Agree scope, acceptance criteria and decision gates before work begins. Review our [commercial models](/company/our-approach#engagement-models) to choose the engagement structure.
